reason: TLC runs out of memory building DOMAIN of a function over 21..2147483647; whether it does depends on the JVM's heap.
evidence: FcnLambdaValue.toFcnRcd allocates its domain and values arrays (new Value[sz]) for the whole interval before it applies the body, about 8.6 GB each for some 2^31 elements; TLC.process catches the OutOfMemoryError and prints EC.SYSTEM_OUT_OF_MEMORY (1001), exit 255. The pinned jar printed 1001 'Java ran out of memory' (exit 255) within 4 s at each heap it was run at (-Xmx512m, 1g, 3g twice, 6g, 8g, G1, no compressed oops, -Xss16m: 9 runs); the same expression with the interval's bound cut to 60,000,000 prints 1001 at -Xmx256m and TLC's own error at -Xmx3g, so the output is a function of the heap, which Prove It doesn't have. Its upstream suite file records 1001 (exit 255), what the jar prints at the corpus's -Xmx3g; an array of 2^31 - 21 to 2^31 - 3 elements is within HotSpot's limit, so above a heap of roughly 9 to 43 GB TLC goes on to its own result. tla-ts tags it tlc-bug and checks its 'correct' (unbounded heap) output instead. Prove It declines.

reason: After a StackOverflowError, the call stack TLC prints depends on how many of CallStackTool's pops themselves overflowed on the way out, which depends on the JVM's stack size and on which frames the JIT has compiled.
evidence: CallStackTool.eval/evalAppl push each node and pop it in a finally block (CallStack.pop); StackOverflowError is not caught there, so a pop that overflows again leaves its entry and CallStack.toString prints the outermost entries left. The upstream suite file records 'The error call stack is empty.', and the jar sometimes prints one position instead ('0. Line 15, column 9 to line 15, column 13'): the pinned jar printed the one position in 1 of 11 runs at the corpus's settings (-Xmx3g -Xss2m), 3 of 13 in another series, and 2 of 20 over -Xss256k..16m, -Xint, C1 only and no tiered compilation, printing 'The error call stack is empty.' otherwise. tla-ts always prints the empty stack. Prove It declines ('recursion too deep').
